label: Signed Offer
description: The countersigned offer letter that triggers onboarding: the new hire's name, role title, department, start date, and manager. The document the whole workflow starts from.

lesson.intent: Inspect the signed offer and tag the fields the workflow depends on - role, start date, and manager - before anything is provisioned.

labVersion: Inspected by you in the Signed Offer task; the offer is a local document fixture the onboarding record is keyed from.
accessNeeded: Read access to the signed offer
Recruiter handoff of the completed offer
Agreement on which fields are authoritative
soloRebuildPath: Start with the signed offer as a local document fixture
Tag the fields onboarding needs: role, start date, manager
Later trigger from the ATS or e-signature webhook
governanceNote: The start date on the signed offer is the authoritative clock; every SLA in the plan is measured backward from it.
auditNote: Inspection by tagging (tagSource): the learner tags each field in the offer, minting a source profile the onboarding record trusts.

label: Role Profile Catalog
description: The governed catalog of what each role gets on day one: accounts, software, hardware, access groups, and payroll class. The provisioning matrix People Ops owns.

lesson.intent: Read the role profile catalog as governed reference data: who owns it, why it is the single source for what a role gets, and how least-privilege is baked in.

labVersion: Provided as a local role-profile catalog fixture the provisioning plan and access task expand from.
accessNeeded: Read access to the role catalog
People Ops Lead ownership of changes
soloRebuildPath: Start with a local table of role -> entitlements
Record who owns each entitlement change
Later integrate with the access-management system
governanceNote: The People Ops Lead owns the catalog; access is granted by role, not by request, so least-privilege is the default and every grant is traceable to a profile.
auditNote: Governance lesson; the temporal loop (onboarding-archive -> role-profile-catalog) refines this catalog from what past hires actually needed.

label: Onboarding Record
description: The master record for one hire, built from the signed offer: who they are, their role, department, start date, and manager. The record every provisioning branch reads.

lesson.intent: Build the master onboarding record from the signed offer - the trusted structured record the whole workflow acts on instead of the letter.

labVersion: Built by you in the Onboarding Record task from the signed offer fixture.
accessNeeded: Agreement on the required record fields
Write access to the onboarding system
soloRebuildPath: Hand-key the offer fields into one JSON record
Validate role, start date, and manager are present
Later create it automatically from the ATS trigger
governanceNote: The onboarding record is what the workflow trusts instead of the offer letter; its start date drives every downstream SLA.
auditNote: Build lesson; every provisioning branch and the readiness gate reads this record, so its fields must be owned and stable.

label: SLA Policy
description: The governed deadlines for each provisioning task, expressed in business days relative to the start date (for example accounts by SD-2, badge by SD-1). What 'on time' means for onboarding.

lesson.intent: Read the SLA policy as owned, versioned config: per-task deadlines measured backward from the start date, not numbers buried in someone's head.

labVersion: Provided as a local SLA-policy fixture the provisioning plan and readiness gate apply.
accessNeeded: People Ops Lead approval for changes
soloRebuildPath: Start with a local policy of task -> business-days-before-start
Version it and record who approved each deadline
Later wire it into the workflow tool's due dates
governanceNote: SLA deadlines are People Ops-approved and versioned; a shorter SLA buys margin before day one but strains the provisioning teams.
auditNote: Governance lesson; the hard tier deepens this into designing the SLA policy from past onboarding completion times.

label: Provisioning Plan
description: The task list for one hire: the role profile expanded into concrete provisioning tasks, each with an owner and an SLA date. The plan the four branches execute in parallel.

lesson.intent: Expand the role profile into a concrete task list, attaching each task's owner and its SLA date computed from the start date.

labVersion: Built by you in the Provisioning Plan task from the onboarding record, role profile, and SLA policy fixtures.
accessNeeded: The onboarding record and role profile
A place to create owned tasks
soloRebuildPath: Expand the role's entitlements into one task each
Attach an owner and an SLA date to every task
Later generate tasks in the workflow tool automatically
governanceNote: The plan turns a role into accountable work: every task has one owner and one SLA date, so nothing is 'someone will handle it'.
auditNote: Central transformation; it fans out to the four parallel task branches - the map's widest simultaneous opening.

label: Accounts Task
description: Create the new hire's core accounts - identity, email, directory - once. Running it twice must not create two accounts: the branch that teaches idempotency.

lesson.intent: Create accounts idempotently: check for an existing identity first so a re-run after a partial failure never creates a duplicate account.

labVersion: Run by you in the Accounts Task using the provisioning plan; the identity store is a local fixture you check before creating.
accessNeeded: IT Provisioner rights in the identity provider
A way to look up existing accounts
soloRebuildPath: Look up the hire before creating an account
Create only if none exists; otherwise reuse it
Later wire the identity provider's provisioning API
governanceNote: Idempotency is the safety rule of automated provisioning: a re-run must converge to one account, never two, or offboarding and audit break.
auditNote: Transformation; the medium tier re-runs this after a partial failure to prove the check-then-create rule holds.

label: Hardware Task
description: Order, track, and confirm the new hire's laptop - a physical-world task the automation cannot complete itself. It hands off to Facilities and captures the shipment confirmation.

lesson.intent: Hand off the physical laptop provisioning: place the order, name the owner, and capture the tracking confirmation the tracker needs.

labVersion: Worked by you in the Hardware Task; the order and its confirmation are captured as a handoff record.
accessNeeded: The hire's start date and ship-to
A place to capture the tracking number
soloRebuildPath: Place the laptop order against the plan
Capture owner, order id, and expected date
Later wire the asset-management ordering API
governanceNote: Some tasks end in the physical world; the automation's job is to trigger, track, and capture confirmation, not to pretend it shipped the box.
auditNote: Handoff (handoffForm): captures who ordered, the tracking id, and whether it lands before the start date; medium tier backorders it.

label: Access Task
description: Grant the systems and building access the role needs - and only what the role needs. Access groups are read straight from the role profile, never invented per hire.

lesson.intent: Grant access by expanding the role profile's access groups, enforcing least-privilege so no hire gets more than their role defines.

labVersion: Run by you in the Access Task from the role profile's access groups; the grant is validated against the profile.
soloRebuildPath: Read the access groups from the role profile
Grant exactly those, nothing extra
Later wire the identity-governance system
governanceNote: Least-privilege is enforced by sourcing access from the role profile: a grant the profile does not list is a policy violation, not a convenience.
auditNote: Transformation; reuses role-profile-catalog, reinforcing that access is governed by role, not by request.

label: Payroll Task
description: Enroll the new hire in payroll for their pay class - a handoff to the Payroll Specialist that must return a captured confirmation before day one.

lesson.intent: Hand off payroll enrollment: send the pay class and start date to Payroll and capture the enrollment confirmation the tracker needs.

labVersion: Worked by you in the Payroll Task; the enrollment request and its confirmation are captured as a handoff record.
accessNeeded: The hire's pay class and start date
A place to capture the confirmation
soloRebuildPath: Send pay class and start date to Payroll
Capture the enrollment id and confirmation
Later wire the HRIS-to-payroll integration
governanceNote: A payroll handoff without a captured confirmation is a dropped ball; the new hire must be enrolled before their first cycle.
auditNote: Handoff (handoffForm): captures the pay class, receiver, and confirmation; parallels the hardware handoff on the human side.

label: Task Tracker
description: One status record across the four parallel branches: each task's state (pending, in-progress, done, blocked) with a reason when blocked. The single source the gate reads.

lesson.intent: Record the state of all four provisioning tasks on one tracker, setting each task's state from its branch's event and a reason when blocked.

labVersion: Built by you in the Task Tracker task by setting each task's state row from the four branch outcomes.
soloRebuildPath: List the four tasks with a state each
Set state from the branch outcome; add a reason if blocked
Later sync states from the workflow tool automatically
governanceNote: The allowed states are fixed (pending, in-progress, done, blocked); a blocked state without a reason hides the problem the gate needs to see.
auditNote: Transformation via jsonDeltas rows (taskId/state/blockedReason); the fan-in the readiness gate evaluates on ALL.

label: Readiness Gate
description: The fork: if every task is done within its SLA the hire is Day-One Ready and the package is assembled; if any task is blocked or past SLA, the hire is escalated. Fan-in on ALL.

lesson.intent: Encode the readiness rule: assemble the package only when ALL four tasks are done inside SLA; any blocked or late task routes to escalation.

labVersion: Encoded by you in the Readiness Gate task from the task tracker's four states.
soloRebuildPath: Read all four task states
Ready only if every one is done within SLA
Otherwise route the whole hire to escalation
governanceNote: The gate is ALL, not most: one blocked task blocks the hire no matter how many others are done - the orchestration invariant the module exists to teach.
auditNote: The single decision node (the fork); boundary case done-at-deadline passes. Hard tier is the solo-rebuild capstone (artifactImport).

label: Escalation Path
description: The worklist for a hire the gate could not clear: name the blocked task, its owner, and a deadline to resolve, so a stuck onboarding is escalated instead of silently late.

lesson.intent: Escalate a blocked task: capture which task is blocked, the accountable owner, and the resolution deadline before day one.

labVersion: Worked by you in the Escalation Path task; the escalation is captured as a handoff record from a blocked tracker.
accessNeeded: The blocked task and its reason
A place to record the escalation
soloRebuildPath: Name the blocked task and why
Assign an owner and a resolution deadline
Later wire the escalation into the ticketing system
governanceNote: Every escalation captures an owner and a deadline; a blocked task with no named owner is how a start date quietly slips.
auditNote: Handoff (handoffForm) with captured owner and deadline; deepens Module 1's escalation ladder under orchestration.

label: Day-One Package
description: The readiness certificate: every provisioning task done or explicitly escalated, assembled the evening before the start date and traceable to the plan and tracker. The module's deliverable.

lesson.intent: Assemble the Day-One Ready certificate from the plan and tracker, listing every task's outcome so the hiring manager can trust the hire is ready.

labVersion: Assembled by you in the Day-One Package task from the provisioning plan and the completed task tracker.
accessNeeded: The plan and the final tracker
A place to deliver the certificate
soloRebuildPath: List every task with its final outcome
Note any escalation and its status
Assemble the certificate the evening before start
governanceNote: The package is only trustworthy if it is traceable: every 'done' must point to the task record that proves it, and every exception must be named, not hidden.
auditNote: The assembly node and the module deliverable (day-one-package.md); templateSlots renders it from canon values.

label: Manager Handoff
description: The hiring manager receives the Day-One Package and acknowledges the hire is ready. The captured acknowledgement closes the loop with the person who owns the new hire's first day.

lesson.intent: Hand the package to the hiring manager and capture their acknowledgement - who confirmed readiness and when.

labVersion: Captured by you in the Manager Handoff task from the delivered Day-One Package.
accessNeeded: A place to record the acknowledgement
soloRebuildPath: Deliver the package to the hiring manager
Capture who acknowledged and when
Later wire the acknowledgement into the onboarding tool
governanceNote: A delivery without a captured acknowledgement is not a handoff; the hiring manager's confirmation is the proof the hire is truly owned on day one.
auditNote: Handoff (handoffForm) capturing the acknowledger and timestamp; mirrors Module 2's run-approval sign-off on the delivery side.

label: Onboarding Archive
description: The retained record of the completed onboarding: the package, the tracker, and any escalations. It preserves the run for audit and feeds improvements back to the role catalog.

lesson.intent: Archive the completed onboarding for retention and export what it teaches, so the role catalog can learn what this role actually needed.

labVersion: Archived by you in the Onboarding Archive task from the acknowledged Day-One Package.
soloRebuildPath: Write the completed onboarding to a dated archive
Export what this role needed to the feedback loop
Later integrate with the records system
governanceNote: Retention length is a compliance decision; the archive is also what makes the catalog improve, so it is a loop input, not a dead end.
auditNote: The archive origin of the temporal loop (onboarding-archive -> role-profile-catalog), refined by profile-feedback.

label: Profile Feedback
description: What the archive teaches the catalog: a hire needed a tool the role profile missed, or never used one it listed. The improvement note that closes the onboarding loop.

lesson.intent: Turn the archived onboarding into a catalog improvement: identify what the role actually needed versus what the profile listed, and propose the change.

labVersion: Run by you in the Profile Feedback task from the onboarding archive fixture.
soloRebuildPath: Compare what the hire needed to the role profile
Write the proposed catalog change
Later feed usage analytics into the review
governanceNote: Catalog changes still go through People Ops governance; feedback proposes, it does not silently rewrite the provisioning matrix.
auditNote: Closes the temporal loop into role-profile-catalog; the improvement is a proposal the catalog owner ratifies.
